pairCriterion: A pair is meaningful when its alternatives reflect distinct, plausible interpretations or calculation errors; mere numerical difference is insufficient.

overall.assessment: Five items have a unique supported option. P02 has none: its expected net gain is -$1.00. P03 is a direct complement of the supplied green probability and meets an explicit level-2 exclusion. P01 is also very easy, though it does not literally match any of the three stated exclusions. P02 and P06 repeat an expected-net-gain decision and monetary answer format. This six-item author-only worksheet is not a reliable level-2 set.

items.answerJustification: One spin cannot land on red and blue simultaneously, so the events are mutually exclusive. Their disjoint probabilities add: 2/5 + 2/5 = 4/5.
items.topicFit: yes: mutually exclusive events and union probability
items.assumptions: The equal sectors and one-spin event definitions are explicit.
items.scenarioConditionUse: The learner must infer disjointness from a single landing and identify four favorable sectors before using the union rule.
items.answerCues: A isolates an incorrect event relationship; C gives only one event's probability; D treats the two 2/5 events like independent intersections. No superficial answer cue is apparent.

A-B.reason: Same union probability but opposite judgment of mutual exclusivity.

A-C.reason: Both event relationship and union calculation differ.

A-D.reason: Same incorrect relationship but union count versus product-like calculation.

B-C.reason: Same correct relationship but union of both colors versus one color alone.

B-D.reason: Correct disjoint union versus incorrect overlap judgment and product-like value.

C-D.reason: Single-color probability with disjointness versus product-like value with incorrect overlap judgment.
